svg.title: From a research question to a study design
svg.desc: 1. Define the knowledge gap. Population, problem, objectives, feasibility and ethical importance.. 2. Choose the approach. Numerical effect or prevalence, lived experience, historical evidence, or mixed methods.. 3. Define variables and outcomes. Conceptual meaning, operational measure, timing and possible confounders.. 4. Choose a suitable design. Compare observational or experimental designs and protect against bias.. 5. Plan analysis and interpretation. Prespecify the question, assumptions and limits to causal inference.

g.text: From a research question to a study design
The question determines the method, not the reverse.
Population, problem, objectives, feasibility and ethical importance.
Numerical effect or prevalence, lived experience, historical evidence, or mixed methods.
Conceptual meaning, operational measure, timing and possible confounders.
Compare observational or experimental designs and protect against bias.
Prespecify the question, assumptions and limits to causal inference.
Random sampling and random allocation serve different purposes.
